elements.title: TOTAL EXTERNAL DEBT STOCK, 2025
elements.description: A headline indicator shows total external debt stock in 2025 and its increase from 2024.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. It rises overall from 4,824 to 5,950, with some fluctuations in the later years.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.description: Nested stacked bars break down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt, then break down public and publicly guaranteed debt by creditor type. Multilateral debt is 2,398, bilateral debt is 2,090, and private creditors account for 18. Other bilateral is the largest named bilateral component at 1,239, while other multilateral is the largest multilateral component at 994.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–22
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four panels cover external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI. The GNI-based panels show lines from 2015 through 2022 against shaded percentile bands; the exports-based panels have no data values. The displayed external debt-to-GNI ratio is 25%, and debt service-to-GNI is 0.0%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Note: Figure 3 shows no data values for the exports-based ratios, or for the GNI-based ratios after 2022. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes are labeled Official creditors and Private creditors. Each lists Maturity, Grace period and Interest rate, with a missing-value marker for each term. There are no arrows or reported values.
elements.notes: Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
